description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.scope: slice 9 progress-stats frontend (implement-progress-stats-ui): the admin stats page /admin/stats (success metric, weekly table, week count, first-try rate per topic, empty state), the admin flag queue /admin/reports (reports with task, reason, note, attached attempt, raw input in full, both verdicts, status filter, re-evaluate, dismiss, outcome line), the admin navigation entries, ISO admin dates, and the admin contract stub's stats and flag queue (src/test/fake-progress-backend.ts)
args.focus: Check against the change's spec delta (openspec/changes/implement-progress-stats-ui/specs/progress-stats/spec.md), the store spec progress-stats (contract/openspec/specs/progress-stats/spec.md: 'Practice statistics page', 'Flag queue', 'Re-evaluation of a reported attempt', 'Dismissing a report', 'Attempt log is append-only', 'Stats and flag queue are admin-only') and contract/api/openapi.yaml for getStats, listReports, reevaluateReport, dismissReport, Stats, WeekStats, Report, LoggedAttempt and ReevaluationResult. Pay attention to: anything the UI computes that the server should own (the metric verdict, sessions, XP), the metric and short-week presentation for every week count and for too little history, raw input shown in full and wrapped (no truncation, no horizontal scroll, U+00A0 kept, locked parts), the outcome messages for every ReevaluationResult shape (changed/unchanged, replay, XP, bonus) and for 409, focus and announcement after an action, the status filter sending only exact contract values, literal UI text bypassing the en catalog (NFR-9), WCAG AA in light and dark (NFR-13), the e2e for FR-40 and FR-41 in chromium, msedge and firefox (NFR-6), and the stub's fidelity to the contract and to the backend half's notes (../scratch/slice9-backend-behaviour.md).

findings.title: A 409 refusal moves no focus, and the pressed button can unmount, dropping focus to <body>
findings.evidence: On 409 the catch block runs `setOutcome((o) => ({ text: '', seq: o.seq }))`. Because `seq` is not bumped, the focus effect (`if (outcome.seq) outcomeLine.current?.focus()`) never runs. It then calls `await reload()`. If the report was already handled elsewhere, it is no longer OPEN, so `ReportEntry` stops rendering its action buttons and the focused Re-evaluate/Dismiss button unmounts. Keyboard focus falls to the document. The spec delta says that after an action 'the outcome SHALL be announced and receive focus'. The only feedback here is the `role="alert"` text, which nothing focuses.
findings.suggestion: Give the error paragraph `tabIndex={-1}` and a ref, and focus it after the error is set (for example with an error sequence counter). Or route the refusal text through the focused outcome line. Add a unit/e2e assertion that the alert has focus after a 409.

findings.title: Short weeks are hidden when the shown weeks are empty but older practice exists (the 'no practice' check only looks at the shown weeks)
findings.evidence: `short: metric && !stats.metricMet && !empty && w.qualifyingSessions < METRIC_SESSIONS` turns off every Short marker when `noPractice(stats)` is true. `noPractice` only checks the weeks in the response (`stats.weeks.every(...)`). If the child practised before the 5-week window, the metric is 'Not met', all four metric weeks have 0 qualifying sessions, and yet no week is marked short. The page also shows 'No practice recorded yet', while `firstTryRateByTopic` can show non-zero resolved counts on the same page. The spec only exempts the 'no practice recorded' case and otherwise requires 'every metric week in the response with fewer than 3 qualifying sessions SHALL be marked as short'.
findings.suggestion: Treat the page as empty only when the topic table also has nothing resolved (every `resolved === 0`). Or keep the Short markers whenever `metricMet` is false and limit the empty state to the explanatory message. Add a test where old practice exists and the visible weeks are all zero.

findings.title: The 'unchanged' outcome always says the attempt is still not correct, which is wrong for other changed:false reasons
findings.evidence: `if (!result.changed) return format(t('admin.reports.unchanged'), { task })`. The catalog string reads 'under the current answer spec the attempt is still not correct'. The stub (and likely the backend) also returns `changed:false` when the attempt was already correct (`wasCorrect`) or when the task already has an outcome at or above the re-evaluated one (`RANK[outcome] <= RANK[stored.taskState]`). In those cases the admin is told something false.
findings.suggestion: Use neutral copy such as 'Nothing changed … the report stays open', or check `result.report.attempt?.reevaluation` and the verdicts to tell 'still wrong' apart from 'already resolved'. Confirm the backend's changed:false cases against the backend notes.

findings.title: The 409 message shows the server's `problem.detail` directly, bypassing the en catalog
findings.evidence: `setError(e.problem?.detail ?? t('admin.reports.alreadyHandled'))` renders whatever English text the backend sends. In the stub this is, for example, 'Only an open report can be dismissed; this one is FIXED.', which includes a raw enum value. NFR-9 requires externalized UI strings. The spec does ask to 'show the server's reason', so this is a judgement call, but the shown text is not under the frontend's control.
findings.suggestion: Map the refusal to catalog strings, for example using the report's new status after the reload ('This report is already Fixed/Dismissed'). Or record a documented NFR-9 exception for server-provided problem details.

findings.title: The part-key column is very narrow and its keys do not wrap under table-layout: fixed
findings.evidence: `.report-parts { table-layout: fixed; }` combined with `.report-parts th:first-child { width: calc(var(--space-8) * 1); }` fixes the Part column to a single spacing step. The key cell `{key}` has no `overflow-wrap`, so a longer part key overflows into the Raw input column instead of wrapping. The spec asks that content wrap inside the entry. Also, `calc(x * 1)` does nothing.
findings.suggestion: Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to the table cells (or at least the first column), and size the column with a token-based min width instead of a fixed `--space-8`.

findings.title: The e2e wrap assertion for long raw input is vacuous for an inline span
findings.evidence: `raw.evaluate((el) => el.getClientRects().length > 1 || el.scrollWidth <= el.clientWidth)` runs on `.report-raw`, which is an inline `<span>`. For inline elements both `scrollWidth` and `clientWidth` are 0, so the second disjunct is always true and the check passes even if the text does not wrap. It also never checks that the text stays inside its table cell or entry, which matters under `table-layout: fixed`.
findings.suggestion: Assert that the span's bounding rect fits inside the `.report-entry` (or the cell) rect, and that `getClientRects().length > 1` at 1280×720 for the 100-code-point input.

findings.title: A failed refetch after an action is ignored while cached data exists, so a stale queue still offers actions
findings.evidence: The screen only renders `LoadState` when `!reports.data`. After `invalidateQueries` in `reload()`, a failed refetch leaves the old data in place with `isError` true. The handled report still shows as OPEN with Re-evaluate/Dismiss, and nothing tells the admin the list is stale. `StatsScreen` follows the same pattern (`if (!stats.data)`).
findings.suggestion: When `reports.isError && reports.data` is true, show a non-blocking alert with a retry button (catalog string).

findings.title: Stale doc comments describe a date format the code no longer produces
findings.evidence: `formatWeek` is documented as returning '"5 Oct 2026"', but it calls `adminDate`, which returns ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Likewise `formatTime` in `src/features/reports/reports.ts:3` says '"5 Oct 2026, 16:20"', while `adminDateTime` returns '2026-10-05 16:20'. Both wrappers are thin pass-throughs.
findings.suggestion: Fix the comments to match the ISO output, or drop the wrappers and call `adminDate`/`adminDateTime` directly.

findings.title: Empty state is decided from the shown weeks only: it hides every Short mark and can say 'No practice recorded yet' when practice did happen
findings.evidence: Spec delta, 'Admin stats page': "When the metric is not met, every metric week in the response with fewer than 3 qualifying sessions SHALL be marked as short … When no practice is recorded the page SHALL show an empty-state message." Code: `const empty = noPractice(stats);` … `short: metric && !stats.metricMet && !empty && w.qualifyingSessions < METRIC_SESSIONS`, and `noPractice` only looks at `stats.weeks.every(w => w.sessions === 0 && …)`, which covers just the served window (5 weeks by default). Example: the child last practised 6 or more weeks ago. With the default 5 weeks every served week is zero, so the page shows 'No practice recorded yet. The figures fill in as the child answers tasks.' (that is false) and marks none of the four metric weeks Short, even though the metric is Not met because of exactly those weeks. Even in the true 'No data yet' case, the requirement text says the four zero metric weeks SHALL be Short. design.md:42 decided otherwise ('no week is singled out as short'), so design and spec disagree. stats.test.ts:74 locks in the suppression.
findings.suggestion: Either mark Short whenever `!metricMet` (drop `!empty`), and word the empty-state copy so it fits the shown window only ('No practice in the weeks shown'), or amend the spec delta so the requirement says that with no practice at all no week is marked Short. Add a test where practice sits outside the window.

findings.title: After a 409 refusal, focus is not moved to the outcome and can fall to <body>
findings.evidence:
Spec delta, 'Admin flag queue': "After an action the outcome SHALL be announced and receive focus: … a refusal (409) shows the server's reason and the queue reloads." Code in the catch branch: `setOutcome((o) => ({ text: '', seq: o.seq }))` leaves seq unchanged, so the focus effect does not run. The reason goes to `

`, which never gets focus. After `reload()` the report is no longer OPEN, so the clicked Re-evaluate/Dismiss button is unmounted and keyboard focus is lost to the document body. The unit test at ReportsScreen.test.tsx:265 checks only the alert text and the reload, not focus. No e2e covers the 409 path.
findings.suggestion: On a 409 (and on other failures), move focus to the alert (give it tabIndex=-1 and focus it), or put the refusal text in the focused outcome line. Add assertions for `toHaveFocus()` in the unit test and in an e2e case for FR-41.

findings.title: The e2e 'wrapped' assertion for long raw input can never fail; wrapping and U+00A0 inputs are not actually checked
findings.evidence: Scenario 'Long raw input': "the whole input is shown, wrapped within the entry, with no ellipsis and no horizontal page scroll". The test runs `raw.evaluate((el) => el.getClientRects().length > 1 || el.scrollWidth <= el.clientWidth)`. `raw` is an inline `<span class="report-raw">`, and for an inline element scrollWidth and clientWidth are both 0, so the second operand is always true and the check passes whether or not the text wraps. LONG_RAW (fake-progress-backend.ts:63) also contains ordinary spaces, so `overflow-wrap: anywhere` is never tested. No test, unit or e2e, renders a long input with no break opportunities, such as a run of digits joined by U+00A0. The unit test at ReportsScreen.test.tsx:126 checks only that the NBSP is preserved, not how it lays out.
findings.suggestion: Assert wrapping on the cell instead, for example `getClientRects().length > 1` on the span, or compare the cell height with its line-height. Add a seed or a test case of 100 code points with no spaces, or joined by U+00A0, and check that the raw box stays within the entry and that `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` holds for the document in all 3 browsers.

findings.title: Dismiss outcome copy differs from the scenario text
findings.evidence: Spec delta scenario 'Dismiss': "THEN \"Report dismissed.\" is announced". Catalog: `'admin.reports.dismissed': 'Report on “{task}” dismissed.'`. design.md:86 also says "Report dismissed.". The store spec makes the copy a design choice, but the delta scenario quotes exact text that the UI does not show.
findings.suggestion: Change the delta scenario (and design.md) to the copy that names the task, or match the catalog to the scenario.

findings.title: Literal list separators and sentence joins are built in code, outside the en catalog (NFR-9)
findings.evidence: `return result.bonusXp > 0 ? `${fixed} ${format(t('admin.reports.bonus'), …)}` : fixed;` joins two sentences in code. `rawText` (reports.ts:10), `row.sizes.join(', ')` (StatsScreen.tsx:107) and `short.map(formatWeek).join(', ')` (StatsScreen.tsx:66) use a hard-coded `', '`. AGENTS.md: "All UI strings externalized (NFR-9)".
findings.suggestion: Add catalog keys such as `admin.common.listSeparator` and `admin.reports.fixedXpWithBonus` (with {xp} and {bonus}), or use Intl.ListFormat with the admin locale.

findings.title: Doc comments still describe the old word-style dates
findings.evidence: stats.ts:73: "A week start … as \"5 Oct 2026\"". reports.ts:3: "\"5 Oct 2026, 16:20\", Europe/Prague". The implementation (format.ts:24-31) and design.md:112 use numeric ISO dates: "2026-10-05" and "2026-10-05 16:20".
findings.suggestion: Update both comments to the ISO format.

findings.title: Stub fidelity: the excerpt cuts UTF-16 code units, the topic list differs, and the re-evaluation rule is simplified
findings.evidence: design.md:133 records the backend note: "`taskPromptExcerpt` is the first 80 code points of the current prompt plus '…'". The stub uses `prompt.slice(0, 80)`, which counts UTF-16 code units. The stub also lists every reference topic in firstTryRateByTopic (line 246), while the backend lists only topics with a published TEXT task (this one is acknowledged in the design). For replay re-evaluation (lines 275-287) the stub requires every part to be CORRECT. The store spec says "If the new verdict is better than the attempt's recorded verdict". I could not read the backend notes file (`../scratch/slice9-backend-behaviour.md`) because it is outside the allowed directories, so the stub was checked only against what design.md says those notes contain.
findings.suggestion: Use `[...prompt].slice(0, 80).join('')`. Optionally filter topics to those with a published TEXT task. Re-read the backend notes before the review gate (task 4.3), as design.md:137 promises.

findings.title: The 'Not re-entered: correct on attempt 1' label appears for any part missing from rawInput
findings.evidence: Backend note (design.md:126): "a part locked as correct on attempt 1 is absent from attempt 2's `rawInput` but has its verdict". Code: `value === undefined ? {t('admin.reports.lockedPart')}` does not check that `attempt.attemptNo === 2` or that `verdict === 'CORRECT'`. A part missing from rawInput for any other reason would be labelled wrongly as locked.
findings.suggestion: Show lockedPart only when the attempt is attempt 2 and the part's verdict is CORRECT. Otherwise show a neutral '—'.

findings.title: Coverage summary
findings.evidence: 13 delta scenarios: 12 implemented, 1 partial (Long raw input: the wrap assertion cannot fail), 0 missing, 0 contradicted. On top of that, 2 requirement statements are not met: Short marks are hidden in the empty state, and focus is not moved after a 409. The UI-facing store scenarios (Practice statistics page, Flag queue, Re-evaluation outcomes, Dismiss, Attempt log both verdicts, admin-only and child UI has no link) are covered by unit and e2e tests on chromium, msedge and firefox at 1280×720 (playwright.config projects). No UI computation duplicates server-owned figures: the verdict comes from `metricMet`, and sessions and XP are shown as served. The status filter sends only OPEN, FIXED or DISMISSED, or no parameter. The weeks parameter is a digit string from the fixed choices. Ticked tasks 1.x–3.x have artifacts on disk (red-run evidence, specs, routes, catalog). 4.x is open, which is correct. The NFR-13 light/dark a11y gates take in both routes through ADMIN_ROUTES; I did not run them here.
findings.suggestion: Fix the three major findings. Then run `CI=1 npm run qa:verify` (task 4.1) to get exit-coded a11y, theme and e2e evidence before ticking 4.x.

result.reasoning:
I confirmed the mechanism in the code. In `ReportsScreen.tsx:59-64`, the catch block runs `setOutcome((o) => ({ text: '', seq: o.seq }))` without bumping `seq`. The effect at lines 45-47 only depends on `outcome.seq`, so it does not run and nothing gets focus. The 409 branch then sets the error and awaits `reload()`, which invalidates `REPORTS_KEY`. A 409 means the report was already handled, so the refetched report is no longer OPEN.
- With the 'OPEN' filter, the whole `<li>` disappears.
- With 'All', `ReportEntry` stops rendering its `admin-actions` div (line 222: `report.status === 'OPEN' &&`).

Either way, the Re-evaluate/Dismiss button that had focus unmounts and focus drops to `<body>`. Nothing guards against this. The `role="alert"` paragraph (lines 97-101) has no ref and no `tabIndex`, and no code focuses it.

The spec claim needs a caveat. `progress-stats/spec.md:63-66` says "the outcome SHALL be announced and receive focus: fixed…, fixed on a replay…, or nothing changed…; a refusal (409) shows the server's reason and the queue reloads." The 409 clause comes after the semicolon, so it is debatable whether the focus requirement covers it. Losing focus to `<body>` when the focused control unmounts is still a real keyboard/a11y defect (WCAG 2.4.3), and it is inconsistent with the success path, which deliberately moves focus.

I'm downgrading the severity because `role="alert"` still announces the refusal to screen readers. Only the focus position is lost, and that happens only on the 409 race.

I confirmed the mechanism in `src/features/reports/ReportsScreen.tsx`.

**What happens on a 409:**
- Line 60 keeps `seq` the same, so the focus effect (lines 45–47) does not run.
- Line 63 then awaits `reload()`, which invalidates `REPORTS_KEY`.
- The backend sends a 409 when the report was already handled (design.md:136). After the refetch, that report is FIXED or DISMISSED.
- `ReportEntry` only shows the action buttons when `report.status === 'OPEN'` (line 222). With the OPEN filter on, the whole list item is removed instead.
- Either way, the focused Re-evaluate or Dismiss button unmounts. Nothing else takes focus, so it falls to `<body>`.

**Can a real user hit it?** Yes. The admin only has to act on a stale list, for example with a second tab open, or after a report was handled elsewhere. Re-evaluating a report with no attempt can also return 409, but the UI hides that button.

**Why I downgraded it:**
- The spec line the finding quotes ("After an action the outcome SHALL be announced and receive focus") lists the success outcomes. It then describes the 409 case separately: "a refusal (409) shows the server's reason and the queue reloads". That clause does not explicitly require focus.
- The refusal is still announced. The `role="alert"` paragraph is inserted with its text, and screen readers read inserted alerts.
- What remains is a real keyboard and accessibility problem: after the refusal, focus drops to the document start. It is not a correctness failure or a clear spec violation, so medium/minor fits better than major.

The finding holds up. In `stats.ts:35`, `empty = noPractice(stats)`, and `noPractice` (`stats.ts:64-65`) only checks the weeks in the response: no sessions, hints or reveals. When that is true, `stats.ts:44` turns off every `short` flag. `shortWeeks` builds on `weekRows`, so the metric's list of short weeks is empty too. `StatsScreen.tsx:31` uses the same check to show the 'admin.stats.empty' message.

The case can really happen. The contract spec (`contract/openspec/specs/progress-stats/spec.md:165-188`) says the response has exactly N weeks, so older activity is not in `weeks`. The first-try rate per topic is counted over all resolved tasks, with no time limit. If the child practised before the window and nothing since, the result is: the metric shows 'Not met', all four metric weeks have 0 qualifying sessions, no week is marked Short, the page says no practice is recorded, and the topic table still shows non-zero resolved counts.

The frontend change spec (`openspec/changes/implement-progress-stats-ui/specs/progress-stats/spec.md:11-13`) says: "When the metric is not met, every metric week in the response with fewer than 3 qualifying sessions SHALL be marked as short." It gives no exception for the empty state. The 'No data yet' scenario only requires zeros, 'Not met', the empty message and no error. It never says to hide the Short markers. So the code breaks the frontend spec in the old-practice case. Arguably it does in the true-empty case as well. The contract spec calls short-week presentation a frontend design choice, but this repo's own spec turned that choice into a SHALL.

Nothing else guards this, and no test covers old practice with all-zero visible weeks. The effect is only on what the admin page shows, so minor severity is right.

The finding is confirmed. In `stats.ts:44`, `short` requires `!empty`. `empty = noPractice(stats)` (line 64–65) is true only when every *served* week has 0 sessions, 0 hints and 0 reveals. It never looks at `firstTryRateByTopic`.

The store spec (`contract/openspec/specs/progress-stats/spec.md:165-178`) limits the weekly figures to the N requested weeks. The first-try rate, by contrast, covers every task "resolved at least once" with no time window. So a response can easily have all-zero weeks, `metricMet=false` and non-zero `resolved` counts.

Real-user scenario: the child practised, then took a break of 5 or more weeks (summer holidays, illness). The admin opens Stats with the default 5 weeks and sees:
- "No practice recorded yet. The figures fill in as the child answers tasks."
- No "Short" chips on any of the four metric weeks, even though each has 0 qualifying sessions and the verdict is Not met.
- No "Short weeks:" list.
- A topic table on the same page with, for example, "75%, 6 of 8 first try".

The empty-state message is then factually wrong, and the frontend change spec's rule is broken: "When the metric is not met, every metric week in the response with fewer than 3 qualifying sessions SHALL be marked as short." That spec only exempts the case where "no practice is recorded", and practice *was* recorded.

The design doc's choice to treat all-zero served weeks as empty does not cover this. It assumes no practice at all ("With no practice at all the empty-state message speaks"). The existing tests (`stats.test.ts:74`, `StatsScreen.test.tsx:119`) only cover a truly empty history.

No other code guards against this: the backend serves exactly N zero weeks for inactive periods (spec line 170–171). The bug needs an ordinary situation, not an edge case. The impact is a misleading admin display with no security or data effect, so the minor severity is right.

I could not refute this. The finding holds.

At `ReportsScreen.tsx:21`, every `changed: false` result is mapped to `admin.reports.unchanged`. In `en.ts:353` that string reads "under the current answer spec the attempt is still not correct". Nothing in the code tells the different no-change reasons apart.

**The contract has `changed: false` cases where that sentence is false.** The progress-stats spec, "Re-evaluation of a reported attempt" (lines 331-358), returns no change whenever "the new verdict would not improve the outcome", not only when the attempt is still wrong. Its own scenarios show this:
- **"Re-evaluation never lowers XP"** (lines 398-400): the reported attempt was marked `CORRECT` and the API returns `changed: false`. "Still not correct" is wrong here, because the attempt was correct when it was logged.
- **"Unchanged spec changes nothing"** (lines 402-406): the report can carry a `CORRECT` attempt. Under the current spec that attempt is correct, yet the admin is told it is not.
- **Outcome already at or above the new one:** the attempt is now correct, but the task already has an equal or better outcome. One way this happens is two reports on the same task, where the first re-evaluation already made it correct on the 1st attempt. The spec says nothing changes, but the message says "not correct", which is false.
- **Replay attempts:** the same applies when the new verdict is not better than the recorded one.

**The test fake does the same.** `src/test/fake-progress-backend.ts` returns `unchanged()` when the task is missing (line 273), when the attempt was already correct (`wasCorrect`, line 280), and when the task's outcome already ranks at or above the new one (`RANK[outcome] <= RANK[stored.taskState]`, line 290).

**Nothing guards against it.** The screen does not look at `report.attempt.verdicts` or `reevaluation` before choosing the copy. The spec only requires that "the admin is told that nothing changed", and the current string adds a reason that the code cannot know.

I'm keeping severity at minor: the problem is only misleading admin copy. No data or XP is affected, and the report still correctly stays OPEN.

I could not refute this one. The admin can get a false message through normal use of the queue.

**The code.** At `ReportsScreen.tsx:21`, any `changed:false` result shows `admin.reports.unchanged`. That string (`src/i18n/en.ts:353`) tells the admin the attempt "is still not correct".

**When the server returns `changed:false`.** The contract (`openapi.yaml:1879`) says only that `changed:false` means "nothing changed and the report stays OPEN". The fake backend (`src/test/fake-progress-backend.ts:271-290`) returns it in four cases:
- the task is missing;
- the re-checked attempt is still wrong;
- the attempt was already correct (`wasCorrect`);
- the new outcome ranks no higher than the stored task state (`RANK`).

Only the second case matches the copy.

**How a real admin reaches the false message:**
1. **A correct attempt gets attached.** `reportProblem` attaches "the latest raw attempt of the current run" (`openapi.yaml:979`) whether or not it was correct. Reports can have the reasons `UNCLEAR_PROMPT` or `OTHER` (`openapi.yaml:1477`). So a child who answers correctly and then flags the prompt as unclear creates an OPEN report with a correct attempt. The screen offers re-evaluate for any OPEN report with an attempt. The re-check returns `changed:false` (`wasCorrect`), and the admin is told the attempt "is still not correct", which is false.
2. **Two reports on one task.** One report covers attempt 1 and another covers attempt 2. Re-evaluating the first raises the task to `CORRECT_FIRST_TRY`. Re-evaluating the second then passes the answer check, but the outcome ranks no higher than the stored state, so the result is `changed:false` and the same false message appears.

**What softens it.** The real backend wasn't checked; only the fake was. But the contract doesn't limit `changed:false` to "still wrong", so the frontend shouldn't assume it. The impact is a misleading admin message only: no data or XP is affected, and the report correctly stays open. Severity stays minor.

The finding is refuted. `ReportsScreen.tsx:62` does show `e.problem?.detail`, but that is what the spec asks for. It is not a correctness bug. 1. **The spec requires it.** The change's own spec, `openspec/changes/implement-progress-stats-ui/specs/progress-stats/spec.md:66`, says "a refusal (409) shows the server's reason and the queue reloads". The design table (`design.md:27`) says the same: "409 shown with the server's reason". Using the server's text with a catalog fallback (`t('admin.reports.alreadyHandled')`) does exactly that. 2. **NFR-9 already makes an exception for server text.** In the project's spec, `openspec/specs/content-authoring/spec.md:155-158` requires every string to come from the catalogs "except content the admin entered or the server sent". So server-provided problem details are a documented exception. No new waiver is needed. 3. **The whole admin app already works this way.** `src/features/admin-access/problem.ts:34` `problemMessage()` returns `problem.detail ?? problem.title`. It is used to show server reasons as-is in `SourcesScreen`, `ImagesEditor`, `PreviewScreen`, `TaskEditorScreen` and `ConflictAlert`. ReportsScreen follows the same pattern, only inline. 4. **Language is not a problem.** The admin UI is English, and so is the backend's `detail`, so there is no language mismatch for the user. **Possible nit:** the `

` at line 98 is not marked `data-content`. The spec says server text should be marked as content. That is a separate tagging point, not the mechanism this finding describes. The finding itself calls this "a judgement call", and the spec settles it in favour of the current code.

The finding describes the code correctly: line 62 renders `e.problem?.detail`, falling back to the catalog string. But this is the specified behaviour, not a defect. `openspec/changes/implement-progress-stats-ui/design.md:87-88` says "a 409 → the server's `detail` (or "This report was already handled.") and the queue reloads". The change's spec delta says "a refusal (409) shows the server's reason" (specs/progress-stats/spec.md:66). The repo also documents this treatment of server text under NFR-9 as an accepted project convention: the authoring-missions design says "Server text (`detail`, `errors[].message`) … are shown as received" (archive/2026-10-05-implement-authoring-missions-ui/design.md:96-97). The shared helper `src/features/admin-access/problem.ts:36` follows the same pattern (`detail ?? title`), and the content-authoring spec requires a 409 alert to show the problem's `detail`. So the "documented NFR-9 exception" the finding asks for already exists. The admin UI is English and the backend's `detail` is English, so no language mismatch can occur either. The finding raises no security or reproducibility problem: the text comes from the authenticated first-party backend and React renders it as text, so there is no injection. What remains is a style preference that contradicts the written design.

The code does what the finding says: at ReportsScreen.tsx:194, `lockedPart` is shown whenever `rawInput[key]` is undefined. `partKeys` (line 121) merges the keys of `verdicts` and `rawInput`, so this only happens when a part has a verdict but no raw input. The finding needs another way for that to happen, and the contract gives none:

- openapi.yaml:192–196 says `submitAttempt` is "Submit all parts of a task" and that only "Parts locked as correct from attempt 1 may be omitted on attempt 2 (OQ-11)".
- An attempt that can't be read is never stored (`status: UNPARSEABLE` → "no attempt was used or stored").
- `LoggedAttempt.verdicts` holds only CORRECT or WRONG.

So a logged attempt can't be missing a part on attempt 1. A part with a verdict but no raw input can only be a part locked as correct on attempt 1, which is the label's exact meaning. design.md:126 says the same, and the test at ReportsScreen.test.tsx:146 covers this case.

The suggested guard (`attemptNo === 2 && verdict === 'CORRECT'`) is defensive against data the contract rules out. It doesn't fix a reachable bug. I found no path where the label is wrong, so the mechanism is not confirmed.

The code does what the finding says. `ReportsScreen.tsx:194` shows lockedPart whenever `rawInput[key] === undefined`. `partKeys` (line 121) takes the union of the verdict keys and the rawInput keys. The finding assumes a part can be missing from rawInput for some other reason, but it names none, and the specs give none.

- The practice-flow design (archive design.md:124) says a submission carries "the answers of every part that is not locked". On attempt 1 nothing is locked, so every part is sent. An empty input is still sent as a string, so it is not undefined.
- The progress-stats design (design.md:74, :126) names locking as the only reason a part has no raw input: "a part locked as correct on attempt 1 is absent from attempt 2's rawInput but has its verdict".
- Only a part that was correct can be locked, so a missing part's verdict is CORRECT by construction. A check on attemptNo or the verdict would therefore never change the output for data the spec allows.

The only way to reach the mislabel is a backend that breaks its own contract. That is not something a real user or attacker can trigger, and the impact would just be a cosmetic label in the admin UI.
